metadata.architecture: six-channel three-head attention-only causal decoder with parameter-free RMS normalization
metadata.author: declarative architecture search
metadata.mechanism_hypothesis: Reducing the residual width from twelve to six while retaining three causal attention heads will test whether the zero-scoring parent contains unused channel capacity that can be removed without lowering public eligibility.
metadata.name: Six-Channel Three-Head RMS Decoder
metadata.research_current_explanation: The twelve-channel attention-only parent scores zero publicly at 756 trusted parameters, so its channel capacity has no observed arithmetic benefit.
metadata.research_decision_rule: Retain the candidate only if it is valid, preserves the frozen public eligibility floor, and reduces trusted parameter count; use public accuracy only for an exact parameter-count tie.
metadata.research_evidence: The current result shows that twelve residual channels and four dimensions per head do not produce measurable public accuracy, while all normalization parameters have already been removed.
metadata.research_expected_result: The six-channel model should preserve the current public eligibility level while substantially reducing trusted parameter count.
metadata.research_next_experiment: Reduce every hidden representation from twelve channels to six while preserving three heads, sinusoidal positions, residual addition, tied readout, and parameter-free RMS normalization.
metadata.research_previous_interpretation: Removing affine RMS gains reduced the trusted parameter count to 756 but left the public score at zero, providing no evidence that the remaining twelve-channel width is useful.
